takeaways: Big Tech's massive AI capital expenditure is pressuring free cash flows and triggering a market rotation toward value and small-cap stocks as investors demand immediate bottom-line returns.

Central banks are diversifying reserves into gold to mitigate geopolitical risk and dollar-denominated debt costs, even as coordinated currency interventions stabilize the Yen and global bond markets.

China's slowing domestic demand and EV price wars contrast with robust European BEV adoption, while AI infrastructure bottlenecks drive a shift toward software-defined power management and advanced semiconductor nodes.

items.title: Gold Erases Early Rally as WGC Reports First-Half Central Bank Buying at Lowest Since 2022
bullets: Central bank gold buying has decelerated to its weakest first-half pace since 2022, signaling a shift toward two-way flows as nations like Russia reduce holdings to finance budget deficits.

The US and Japan recently conducted their first joint currency intervention since 2011, spending over $65 billion to support the Yen, which has contributed to increased volatility in precious metals and broader currency markets.
items.reason: Significant shift in central bank reserve management and rare G7 currency intervention.

items.title: India central bank to stay on hold even as peers pivot to rate hikes
bullets: The Reserve Bank of India is expected to maintain current interest rates this week, diverging from global peers who are pivoting toward hikes to combat persistent inflation risks.

Despite external pressures from oil price shocks and global supply chain disruptions, the RBI remains focused on domestic data, prioritizing economic stability over the tightening cycles seen in other major economies.
items.reason: Diverging monetary policy in a major emerging market impacts carry trade and capital flows.

items.title: Why Gold Is Emerging as the Reserve Asset of a Multipolar Global Economy
bullets: Central banks are increasingly viewing gold as 'outside money' to mitigate geopolitical risks and sanctions, leading to a structural reweighting of reserves away from exclusive reliance on the US dollar.

The paradox of a strong dollar is accelerating this diversification, as higher debt-servicing costs for dollar-denominated debt force reserve managers to seek neutral, non-sovereign assets to reduce long-term balance sheet risk.
items.reason: Structural change in global reserve composition affects long-term currency valuations.

items.title: Here's the single biggest reason the bull market is broadening
bullets: Aggressive capital expenditure by Big Tech to fund AI ambitions is suppressing free cash flow yields, prompting investors to rotate capital into value-oriented sectors and small-cap stocks.
For the first time since 2009, the equally weighted S&P 500 has outperformed the market-cap-weighted index by over 7.3%, signaling a significant shift in market leadership away from hyperscalers.
items.reason: Identifies a major structural shift in equity market leadership and capital allocation.

items.title: SpaceX's first-ever earnings report comes as stock hits new all-time low: Q2 preview
bullets: SpaceX faces a critical test with its first public earnings report, as the stock has plummeted nearly 50% from its all-time high amid concerns over massive capital expenditure requirements and rising debt.

An upcoming lockup expiration on August 6 will release shares equal to triple the current tradable float, creating significant supply-side pressure that investors are monitoring alongside Q2 revenue and Starlink profitability.
items.reason: High-profile IPO facing a critical earnings catalyst and potential liquidity overhang.

items.title: Why the U.S. stepped in after decades to prop up Japan's yen — and what's at stake
bullets: The U.S. participated in a rare joint intervention to support the yen primarily to prevent Japan from selling large quantities of U.S. Treasurys to fund unilateral market operations, which could have destabilized global bond markets.

Japan’s Finance Ministry plans to utilize the Federal Reserve’s FIMA repo facility for future interventions, a strategic shift that allows Tokyo to secure dollar liquidity without forcing the liquidation of its significant Treasury holdings.
items.reason: Direct impact on Treasury market stability and global central bank policy coordination.

items.title: Global Market: Euro zone bond yields decline as falling oil prices boost market sentiment
bullets: German 10-year yields fell 5 basis points to 3.158% as lower oil prices eased inflation expectations, leading markets to price in only 41 basis points of further ECB tightening compared to 44 previously.

The correlation between energy prices and sovereign debt remains a primary driver for European bond markets, with Italian 10-year yields also dropping 6 basis points as investors recalibrate policy expectations following geopolitical developments.
items.reason: Significant shift in European rate expectations driven by energy price volatility.

items.title: How likely is Beijing to walk the talk on boosting consumption?
bullets: China's second-quarter GDP growth slowed to 4.3%, dragging the first-half average to 4.7% and leaving the economy barely within the official 4.5-5% annual target range.
Domestic demand is significantly underperforming, evidenced by a 5.7% decline in fixed-asset investment, an 18% plunge in property investment, and retail sales growth decelerating sharply to 0.2%.
items.reason: Signals critical structural weakness in China's primary growth drivers.

items.title: The World Should Not Ignore China’s Undervalued Currency
bullets: China's current account surplus is estimated to be 6% of GDP when adjusted for misreported investment income and gold imports, suggesting the renminbi is undervalued by 30-35%.

The People's Bank of China is actively intervening in currency markets, purchasing approximately $50 billion in foreign currency monthly to prevent the yuan from strengthening and maintain export competitiveness.
items.reason: Highlights potential for future trade friction and currency policy shifts.

items.title: Hong Kong: Growth seen moderating – UOB
bullets: Hong Kong's GDP growth decelerated to 4.3% year-on-year in 2Q26, with a 0.6% quarterly contraction marking the first decline since 4Q22, signaling a loss of momentum after a strong start to the year.

Despite resilient consumer spending and a 12.7% year-on-year rise in home prices, UOB maintains a cautious 2026 GDP growth forecast of 3.9% due to downside risks from tighter Mainland capital controls and unfavorable base effects.
items.reason: Provides critical macroeconomic data and revised growth outlook for the Hong Kong economy.

items.title: Zhongji Innolight listing is largest Hong Kong IPO since 2019
bullets: Zhongji Innolight raised HKD 53.41 billion in its HKEX debut, marking the largest IPO in Hong Kong since 2019 and highlighting the city's continued role as a hub for dual-listed high-tech firms.

The offering attracted 33 cornerstone investors, including major global institutions like BlackRock, Temasek, and JP Morgan Asset Management, underscoring strong institutional appetite for AI-linked infrastructure providers.
items.reason: Represents a significant capital market milestone and a major liquidity event for the HKEX.

items.title: Big Tech Results Show 'Mixed Shocks,' Market Direction Uncertain
bullets: Market divergence intensified as Microsoft added $450 billion in market cap on AI revenue optimism, while Apple shares dropped 7.4% due to weak quarterly forecasts and concerns over core iPhone growth.

Meta shares fell 8% following warnings that free cash flow could turn negative in the second half, highlighting investor intolerance for high AI infrastructure spending that fails to show immediate bottom-line returns.
items.reason: Divergent earnings results are driving significant volatility and re-evaluations of AI investment strategies.

items.title: Australia ups demands on Big Tech firms to pay for news stories
bullets: The Australian government is introducing legislation to impose a 2.5% levy on digital advertising revenue for platforms like Google, Meta, and TikTok if they fail to secure commercial content deals with local media.

While the levy rate increased from 2.25%, the government narrowed the scope to apply only to digital advertising revenue rather than total local revenue, potentially capping the financial impact for major tech firms.
items.reason: Regulatory shifts in Australia create new compliance costs and potential precedents for global news-payment legislation.

items.title: Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) foundry roadmaps — breaking down TSMC, Intel, Samsung, and GlobalFoundries' approach to next-generation scale-up connectivity
bullets: As AI cluster bandwidth requirements exceed the efficiency of traditional electrical interconnects, the industry is shifting toward Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) to integrate optical engines directly into processor packages.

This transition is critical for major semiconductor foundries like TSMC and Intel, as it addresses the power consumption and signal integrity bottlenecks inherent in scaling AI infrastructure to thousands of accelerators.
items.reason: Highlights a critical hardware bottleneck and technological shift essential for AI infrastructure scaling.

items.title: Alibaba takes aim at OpenAI and Anthropic with Qwen3.8-Max launch
bullets: Alibaba's launch of Qwen3.8-Max represents a direct competitive challenge to leading Western AI models from OpenAI and Anthropic, signaling an intensification of the global race for large language model supremacy.
The release underscores the rapid advancement of Chinese AI capabilities, which may influence market share dynamics and regulatory scrutiny for AI developers operating in international markets.
items.reason: Represents a significant competitive development in the global AI foundation model landscape.

items.title: TSMC Approaching A New Milestone With Its 2nm Process By The End Of 2026 With 100,000 Monthly Wafers; NVIDIA, AMD, & Others Force Manufacturing Acceleration
bullets: TSMC is scaling its 2nm manufacturing process to reach a capacity of 100,000 wafers per month by the end of 2026, driven by aggressive demand from major clients like Nvidia and AMD.

The rapid acceleration of this advanced node is critical for maintaining TSMC's competitive moat, as it seeks to satisfy the massive compute requirements of next-generation AI data center architectures.
items.reason: Critical supply chain update for the global AI hardware ecosystem.

items.title: Samsung SDS launches NPU-as-a-Service offering with FuriosaAI chips in South Korea
bullets: Samsung SDS has introduced an NPU-as-a-Service (NPUaaS) platform in South Korea, utilizing FuriosaAI's 5nm RNGD accelerators to provide enterprises with scalable AI inference infrastructure.

The service allows companies to deploy agentic AI workloads without managing dedicated hardware, leveraging accelerators that deliver 512 teraflops of FP8 compute per unit to optimize total cost of ownership.
items.reason: Signals a shift toward specialized AI inference hardware and cloud-based NPU adoption.

items.title: Price war fears grip China’s EV market after woeful July sales figures
bullets: Major premium Chinese EV manufacturers, including Xpeng, Nio, and Li Auto, all reported month-on-month sales declines in July, signaling a potential cooling in demand for intelligent vehicles.
The synchronized downturn across these key players has intensified investor fears of a renewed, brutal price war as companies struggle to maintain market share amid a broader economic slowdown.
items.reason: Signals potential margin compression and sector-wide instability in the world's largest EV market.

items.title: Europe EV Sales Report: BEVs Jump 50% & Reach 26% Market Share!
bullets: European battery electric vehicle (BEV) registrations surged 50% year-over-year in June to 366,000 units, achieving a record 26% market share and demonstrating strong resilience despite macroeconomic headwinds.

The data reveals a widening divergence between BEVs and plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), with BEVs now capturing 71% of all plugin sales, suggesting that pure electric models are increasingly dominating the European electrification transition.
items.reason: Highlights a significant shift in consumer preference and market growth in a major global automotive region.

items.title: Beyond PUE: Why AI data centers need verifiable performance data
bullets: AI workloads introduce extreme power and thermal volatility that standard monthly reporting fails to capture, creating hidden risks for lenders and investors regarding SLA compliance and asset performance.

With $7 trillion in projected capital outlays by 2030, the lack of granular, independently verifiable operational data is increasing the cost of capital as lenders struggle to accurately price the financial downside of micro-event failures.
items.reason: Highlights a critical systemic risk in AI infrastructure financing.

items.title: Empromptu AI Launches Grid Guard to Stop AI Data Centers From Breaking Their Own Power Infrastructure
bullets: The Grid Guard software solution reduces power volatility by 80% by staggering GPU workload execution, potentially lowering the massive capital expenditure currently required for redundant power infrastructure like batteries and generators.

By smoothing power demand spikes, this technology addresses a major operational bottleneck for AI data centers, offering a software-defined alternative to the industry's current strategy of overbuilding physical power capacity.
items.reason: Identifies a technological solution to the high capital costs of AI power infrastructure.

items.title: Rocket Lab Lands Launch Contract, Space Force Taps Vendors For $981 Million Program
bullets: The U.S. Space Force has awarded contracts totaling $981 million to multiple vendors, signaling a significant expansion in government spending for launch services and orbital capabilities.
Rocket Lab's inclusion in this high-value program highlights its growing competitive position against larger incumbents in the defense and national security launch market.
items.reason: Significant government contract awards impacting competitive landscape

items.title: SpaceX rocket launch to mark Florida’s 50th mission thus far this year
bullets: AST SpaceMobile is utilizing SpaceX to deploy its next generation of BlueBird satellites, which are critical for the company's goal of launching beta cellular-broadband services later this year.

The mission underscores the rapid cadence of commercial space operations, with SpaceX achieving its 50th Florida launch of the year and demonstrating consistent deployment capacity for large phased-array satellites.
items.reason: Operational milestone for a key commercial satellite operator
